newsitem.title: USA: Patterson Dental sees purchases, new products key.
newsitem.headline: Patterson Dental sees purchases, new products key.

text.p: Patterson Dental Co said on Thursday it sees strategic acquisitions and new product introductions as keys to its growth.

"Looking forward, the company's expansion plans focus primarily on strategic acquisitions offering compelling value," the company said in an earnings statement. "A second strategy for growth centers on ongoing new product introductions."
Patterson reported second-quarter fiscal 1997 earnings of $0.36 per share, up from $0.32. Net sales rose 12.6 percent to $161.9 million from $143.7 million in the year-ago quarter.

"Our second-quarter performance was impacted favorably by an eight-percent increase in consumable sales per customer; resilient equipment sales, which rose 10.4 percent over the year-ago quarter; the expansion of our consumable customer base; and the better-than-expected financial contributions of the Colwell acquisition," said Peter Frechette, president and chief executive officer, in the statement.
Patterson said without the Colwell acquisition, the sales increase for the quarter would have been 9.3 percent.
It said equipment sales rose from flat levels seen during the first quarter due to successful new products, including "strong demand" for its KCP 1000 cavity preparation device.

The company also noted that gross margin rose but operating margin for the quarter slipped on higher expenses related to the company's fiscal 1997 first-quarter conversion of preferred stock to common stock owned by its Employee Stock Ownership Plan. It said the ESOP now will be funded through a charge to operating expense rather than through preferred stock dividends. It estimated that annual charge at $800,000.
Patterson Dental distributes dental products in North America. Its Colwell division makes and sells stationery and office paper products to health care providers.
